July 23, 2026

House passes war powers resolution to curb Trump's Iran war as Republicans break ranks

tags: politics, war, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

The House of Representatives passed a war powers resolution seeking to limit the president's ability to continue military action in Iran, with Republicans Fitzpatrick, Davidson, Massie and Barrett voting against the president. The vote is largely symbolic but signals that Republicans are not united behind the war, and the White House is reported to be angry about it. Separately, Representative Thomas Massie said the Pentagon is treating the campaign as two separate wars divided by a brief cease-fire in order to avoid the 90-day authorization requirement, and accused the Secretary of War of breaking the law. Massie's comments followed reporting that the Pentagon removed four service members who died in Jordan from its official casualty list on the grounds that their deaths occurred after the April cease-fire declaration.

Iranian strike reported on US air base in Kuwait

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Reports describe a deadly Iranian strike on a US military base at Ali Al-Salem in Kuwait, which the Pentagon has not confirmed. Open source reporting cites Iranian satellite imagery showing at least five barracks destroyed, imagery that has not been contested; if confirmed and the barracks were occupied, there would have been casualties. Analysis of the escalation holds that Iran wants to retain leverage over the Strait of Hormuz and claim it made the United States pay for the death of its supreme leader, while the president cannot be seen to walk away. National average gasoline prices have reached $4.09 a gallon.

Houthi strikes close second chokepoint as oil returns to $100 a barrel

tags: markets, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iran-backed Houthi forces said they struck two Saudi oil tankers and began firing missiles and drones into the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which they describe as enforcing a blockade on Saudi ships in response to recent Saudi attacks on Yemen. The strait carries roughly 12% of global trade and had become the route by which Saudi Arabia exported most of its oil after the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed. Maritime insurers are declining coverage, and ships diverting around the Cape of Good Hope add 10 to 18 days to voyages and could more than double shipping costs. Brent crude climbed 4.8% to $98.59 a barrel, with prices reported back at $100.

Trump tells communities they cannot fight data centers

tags: politics, tech, climate
sources: @aaronparnas, @ericmoutsos

The president told an audience of governors and officials that communities cannot fight data centers and must embrace them, arguing the projects bring jobs, local investment, revenue that can eliminate property taxes, and little disruption, and claiming foreign nations are funding public relations campaigns to slow the buildout. Communities across the country are organizing against data centers over air pollution and water use, including a proposed Utah project described as larger than Manhattan. Critics of the remarks noted the tension between saying communities must be convinced and saying they are begging for the facilities.

Musk and Bezos press plan for more than a million orbital data centers

tags: tech, climate
sources: @aaronparnas

SpaceX and Blue Origin are advancing plans to place more than a million data centers in orbit. Experts warn the scheme would generate substantial pollution from satellites and rockets burning up on re-entry, releasing soot, rare metals, aluminium oxides and other compounds with unknown effects. A petition filed by Earthjustice cites scientists who believe the pollution could destroy the ozone layer and could also settle back onto the earth.

Epstein survivor's family urges senators to reject Todd Blanche as attorney general

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Amanda and Sky Roberts, the family of Virginia Roberts Giuffre, released an open letter to two Republican senators urging them to vote against Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general and asking to meet with them alongside other survivors. The letter calls the vote a defining moment and asks the senators to vote no. The White House is reported to be scrambling to secure the votes, and the nomination may not currently have the support to pass.

Existing Epstein files described as sufficient to open dozens of investigations

tags: legal, politics
sources: @cancel.ian.carroll

The publicly available Epstein files are said to contain enough evidence to open many investigations and hold dozens of perpetrators accountable, with the original investigation obstructed from within beginning in 2006 and 2007. Investigators never raided the New Mexico ranch where much of the worst abuse is believed to have occurred, and did not raid the island until August 2019, after Epstein's death. During the 2019 raid on his New York townhouse, agents photographed binders of discs and hard drives appearing to hold blackmail material but did not seize them as outside the warrant's scope; the material was gone when they returned days later and only partially resurfaced via Epstein's own attorney.

SAVE Act attached to emergency Iran funding package via budget loophole

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Republicans have folded a version of the SAVE Act into a $95 billion emergency funding bill covering the Iran conflict and domestic support including agriculture. Because the package allots $10 billion for election infrastructure such as identification-checking systems, the provision is being treated as budget-related and would need only 51 votes in the Senate rather than a filibuster-proof majority. The Senate parliamentarian will have to rule on what qualifies, and attaching the measure to funding for troops abroad adds political pressure on members of both parties.

Trump says he will be crying at home if Republicans keep the filibuster

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The president said he would sit at home and cry if Senate Republicans do not terminate the filibuster and pass his Save America Act agenda, arguing that Democrats would otherwise do so and gain roughly 40 electoral votes by making the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico states. There is not currently enough support among Senate Republicans to eliminate the filibuster.

Only one Republican opposed the NDAA rule vote that let the bill advance

tags: politics, defence
sources: @ericmoutsos

Seven Republicans voted against final passage of the National Defense Authorization Act over Section 219 and other provisions, but only Thomas Massie voted against the procedural rule that allowed the bill to reach the floor. The rule vote passed 213 to 212, meaning the bill could not have advanced had the other six Republicans joined Massie. Six Democrats voted in favour of final passage, making the later Republican no votes non-decisive.

Case against striking Iran laid out on intelligence and military grounds

tags: war, politics
sources: @ericmoutsos

The argument holds that decades of warnings that Iran is about to obtain a nuclear weapon have not come to pass, and that the officials pressing for confrontation are the same ones who advocated the Iraq war. It contends the United States is economically vulnerable, citing de-dollarisation, a difficult tariff-driven manufacturing pivot, depleted military reserves after Ukraine, and the rise of China. Iran is described as a far harder adversary than Iraq or Afghanistan, with 90 million people, mountainous terrain, and decades of preparation including drones, speedboats and cheap expendable weapons, and it is questioned whether an Iranian nuclear weapon would threaten the United States rather than Israel.

ICE to resume vehicle stops nationwide under new internal conditions

tags: immigration, policing
sources: @oafnation_actual

According to DHS whistleblowers citing an internal ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations memo, vehicle stops will officially resume nationwide where deemed operationally necessary. Stops will be permitted only by officers who have completed federal vehicle stop training, and at least one officer present must have an issued and activated body-worn camera. Stops will also be allowed where tied to a criminal arrest or search warrant with a special response team officer on scene.

CDC website edited to question vaccine and autism evidence

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A page on the official CDC website has been changed to state that the claim vaccines do not cause autism is not evidence-based because studies have not ruled out the possibility. Critics say the edit conflicts with peer-reviewed research and is dangerous because official government pages are treated as authoritative sources. A particular concern raised is that students researching the question through AI chat tools will be served the government wording.

Education Department rule would cut student loans for low-earning degree programs

tags: politics, education
sources: @aaronparnas

The Department of Education is rolling out an accountability test under which an undergraduate program whose graduates do not earn more than workers who never attended college could lose access to federal student loans. Officials frame it as the federal government declining to underwrite degrees that do not raise earnings. Critics say the rule could disqualify teaching programs in states such as Florida as well as many liberal arts degrees. The department is moving quickly and the rule could take effect as early as next year.

Utah data center next to Great Salt Lake draws bipartisan opposition

tags: climate, politics, tech
sources: @carolinegleich

Kevin O'Leary's proposed data center in Box Elder County, next to the Great Salt Lake, has met sustained public opposition that has already forced a reduction in the size of the plans and contributed to some Republicans losing office. Critics say the project was advanced through a quasi-governmental agency without any public comment period or environmental review. Opponents describe the fight as unusually unifying, drawing together Republicans, ranchers and farmers alongside other residents.

McConnell has not been seen publicly for more than 39 days as Kentucky filing deadline approaches

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

Mitch McConnell is reportedly still a patient at George Washington University Hospital, more than 39 days after entering by ambulance, with vehicles resembling a security detail outside and staff declining to give information. Under the 2026 Kentucky election calendar, Tuesday 11 August 2026 is the last day for candidates to file a petition for a vacancy arising after the June filing deadline. It is argued that this deadline is why any announcement about McConnell's status would be expected the following week.

Record 105.8 million Americans out of the labor force

tags: markets, economy
sources: @oafnation_actual

The number of Americans not participating in the labor force climbed to a record 105.8 million in June, exceeding the peak reached during the COVID-19 pandemic. Traders are pricing in a 12% probability that the US unemployment rate rises to 5% at some point in 2026.

Trump ties US-Saudi nuclear agreement to Saudi entry into Abraham Accords

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The president said a proposed nuclear agreement between the United States and Saudi Arabia depends on Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords. Any deal would still require approval from Congress.

Five Palestinians killed in Gaza airstrike and West Bank violence

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Five Palestinians were killed on Thursday in an Israeli airstrike in Gaza and in separate violence in the occupied West Bank, according to officials.

Greece approves $4 billion Israeli air-defense system

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Greece approved the purchase of a $4 billion Israeli air-defense system as part of a broader military modernization plan.

Republicans push Save Our Bacon Act to void state animal welfare laws

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Republicans in Congress are advancing the Save Our Bacon Act, which would invalidate state laws requiring that farm animals have room to turn around, lie down and extend their limbs. The provision is pending in the Farm Bill, which senators are marking up and expect to consider in the weeks before the midterm elections. Hundreds of veterinarians have joined calls for Congress to reject the measure.

West Virginia Republican delegate charged with attempting to entice a minor

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Elliot Pritt, a Republican delegate in West Virginia who had campaigned on protecting children from the LGBTQIA and drag community, has been arrested and charged with attempting to entice a 15-year-old minor. The charges relate to contact made on Roblox and Snapchat.

FDA notice covers recall of more than 1.5 million dozen eggs over salmonella risk

tags: health
sources: @aaronparnas

Midwest Poultry Services voluntarily recalled 1,589,577 dozen white shell and brown cage-free shell eggs over possible salmonella contamination, according to a new FDA notice. Affected cartons carry sell-by or best-by dates between 20 July and 17 August and identifying codes P1950 or 0840962 with Julian dates between 157 and 184. The eggs went to food service customers in Texas, Oklahoma and Louisiana and to retailers including Kroger stores in Texas and Louisiana and Brookshire stores across several southern states.
